description: "Use to design, redesign, critique, audit, polish or animate a frontend: websites, landing pages, dashboards, app UI, components, native iOS/Android screens, or a design system (DESIGN.md)."
version: 4.10.0

- Verify by looking at the rendered result at the sizes it ships at (web: `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable shot <page>`), and batch the checks: fix what one look shows before looking again.

1. Run `<skill-base-dir>/scripts/impeccable context` once per session, where `<skill-base-dir>` is the directory that contains this SKILL.md (the skill folder, not a plugin root two levels above it); keep cwd at the user's project. That base directory resolves every `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable <verb>` command in this skill and its references, and `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts` is the fallback only when the runtime reports no base directory. On a Windows shell without `sh`, call `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable.cmd` instead. The launcher runs a self-contained binary that ships next to it or is downloaded once on first run; no Node or other runtime is required. Pass a named source file or route as `--target <path>`. It loads PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md (long ones as a map: read the sections your task needs), the matching surface brief, and native-platform guidance when applicable; follow its directives and do not rerun it.
2. Load the request's playbook: its Commands-table reference for an explicit/implied sub-command, or [reference/new-work.md](reference/new-work.md) for a new surface, a replacement visual world, or a build from an approved comp. Some playbooks come in parts; read the part this request needs in the same step: [reference/new-work-world.md](reference/new-work-world.md) when a visual world is created or replaced (a redesign, a new look, or no established world), [reference/new-work-comp.md](reference/new-work-comp.md) for a build from an approved comp or on a comp-led build path, and [reference/critique-rubric.md](reference/critique-rubric.md) for a critique whose Assessment A runs in this context (a native platform, or no sub-agent tool); a delegated Assessment A gets the rubric's path in its prompt instead. Inspect target and incumbent visual truth before editing. When the app cannot run, start with committed visual-regression goldens or screenshot fixtures; verify target and freshness against current tokens, CSS, components, or assets, resolve conflicts, and compare theme/variant captures.

**Launcher unavailable:** On the first refusal or failure, don’t retry; send a separate message **before the next tool call**: “Context loading did not run; I’ll read the existing project context directly.” Then read existing PRODUCT.md and DESIGN.md without inventing missing context, follow applicable steps 2–3, including reading [reference/craft-floor.md](reference/craft-floor.md) immediately before any UI edit, and continue through permitted tools. This applies to planning and editing; launcher failure alone does not block either.

**Foundations:** `/impeccable foundations` runs `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable foundations` and walks the user through the product-foundations roadmap (secrets, 404 page, icons, CI and more); `/impeccable foundations <id>` fixes that one item. Load [reference/foundations.md](reference/foundations.md) when the user invokes it.
- Bottom nav bar for mobile web
.card:hover .card-surface { transform: translateY(-2px); }  /* Lift a child; the card stays the hit area */
- **Contrast issues**: Text contrast ratios < 4.5:1, or < 3:1 for large text (or 7:1 for AAA)

- **Touch targets**: Interactive elements < 44x44px. WCAG AA (SC 2.5.8) requires at least 24x24 CSS px unless an exception applies: spacing, an equivalent control, inline text, user-agent styling, or an essential size. Spacing passes when a 24 CSS px circle centered on the target's bounding box overlaps no other target and no other undersized target's circle

On RTL-declared pages, each of the following is a signal to verify the rendered result, not a defect in itself; flag only where the rendering is actually wrong:
- **Physical directional properties**: `margin-left/right`, `padding-left/right`, `text-align: left/right`, `float: left/right`, `border-left/right` where logical equivalents (`margin-inline-start/end`, `padding-inline-start/end`, `text-align: start/end`, `float: inline-start/end`, `border-inline-start/end`) would be expected. A direction-scoped override like `[dir="rtl"] .x { margin-right:1rem }` is correct only when it also clears the conflicting base property (e.g. `margin-left: 0`); without that, both margins apply
- **Physical positioning on positioned elements**: `left:` or `right:` instead of `inset-inline-start` / `inset-inline-end`. Note: `left:50%; transform:translateX(-50%)` is a direction-agnostic centering pattern that works correctly in both LTR and RTL; replacing `left` with `inset-inline-start` there breaks the centering because `translateX` is physical and does not mirror
- **Directional icons and assets**: arrows, chevrons, and navigation icons that point the wrong direction for the reading order. An RTL-only page may ship assets already drawn correctly without a `[dir="rtl"]` flip; verify the rendered icon rather than assuming a missing `transform: scaleX(-1)` is a defect

**RTL scope**: flag physical directional properties only on pages that declare `dir="rtl"` on the `<html>` or `<body>` element. A `lang` attribute alone does not set direction (browsers take direction from `dir`, never from `lang`), but treat an RTL-script `lang` (`ar`, `fa`, `ur`, `ps`, `ckb`, `he`, `yi`, `ug`, `sd`, `dv`) without an explicit `dir` as a signal worth noting.

**Score 0-4**: 0=Desktop-only (breaks on mobile), 1=Major issues (some breakpoints, many failures), 2=Partial (works on mobile, rough edges), 3=Good (responsive, minor touch target or overflow issues), 4=Excellent (fluid, all viewports, proper touch targets, gestures work under touch). On RTL-declared pages, reduce by 1 for pervasive rendered RTL failures

## Save the Report

After the report is delivered, save a copy so the findings outlive this conversation: write it, from the score table through Recommended Actions, to a temp file, then run the write command with the scores as metadata and delete the temp file:

```bash
IMPECCABLE_REPORT_META='{"target":"<user phrasing, or .>","total_score":<n>,"max_score":20,"p0_count":<n>,"p1_count":<n>,"p2_count":<n>,"p3_count":<n>}' \
  .claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable audit-storage write "<resolved target, or . for the whole project>" <temp-file>
```

The helper prints the path it wrote, which you mention in one line; `REPORTS OFF:` means the project opted out, and you mention nothing. Saving never replaces delivering: the user reads the report in chat first.

After the report is delivered, save a copy so the findings outlive this conversation: write it, from the score table through Recommended Actions, to a temp file, then run the write command with the scores as metadata and delete the temp file:

```bash

```

The helper prints the path it wrote, which you mention in one line; `REPORTS OFF:` means the project opted out, and you mention nothing. Saving never replaces delivering: the user reads the report in chat first.

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here except a line marked as a ban; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render (on the web, one `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable shot <page or url>`), not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.
- A bar down one side of a rounded box (a one-sided border, inset shadow or pseudo-element), any colour or state. Use a full border, a tint, or a leading icon or label.

- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering (Google: `.claude/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable font-fetch <Family>`); the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.

- If and only if sub-agents are unavailable, fall back sequentially: read [critique-rubric.md](critique-rubric.md) now, finish and record Assessment A, then run Assessment B, then synthesize, and emit the degraded banner.

**Read-only or delegated run.** When this critique runs where it cannot spawn agents, write inside the reviewed repository, or ask anyone (a delegated subagent, CI, a headless call), run it this way rather than improvising (native platforms keep their own path above, which has no banner): read [critique-rubric.md](critique-rubric.md), then Assessment A inline, led by `⚠️ DEGRADED: single-context (delegated read-only run)`; Assessment B as `detect --json` on the sources plus `detect --json <url> --viewport <WxH>` at each target viewport (390x844 for phone), with no live-server or overlay; no Persist the Snapshot, said in Run Notes; and `Questions skipped: delegated run` in place of Ask the User.
- **Cognitive load**: consult the Cognitive Load Assessment in [critique-rubric.md](critique-rubric.md); report checklist failures and decision points with >4 visible options.

- **Nielsen heuristics**: consult the Heuristics Scoring Guide in [critique-rubric.md](critique-rubric.md); score all 10 heuristics 0-4, marking any heuristic the mode-applicability rule allows as `n/a` instead of forcing a number.

- **Persona red flags**: select personas with the Selecting Personas table in [critique-rubric.md](critique-rubric.md), plus 1-2 project-specific ones from PRODUCT.md's `## Users` when it has one, and walk each through the primary action.

Read critique-rubric.md as part of Assessment A. When a sub-agent runs A, give it the file's path so it reads the rubric itself, and the parent does not load it. When A runs in this context (native critiques, or the single-context fallback), read the rubric here before scoring.
- Exit code 0 = no findings; 2 = findings. Report an empty result with what was scanned (files, URLs, viewports), never as clean: the detector does not judge layout.
> *Use Assessment A's scores; the bands are under [Scoring the report](#scoring-the-report) below.*

> *Use Assessment A's persona red flags; it selected the personas from [critique-rubric.md](critique-rubric.md).*

Assessment A selected 2-3 personas most relevant to this interface type (the selection table in critique-rubric.md). If PRODUCT.md has a `## Users` section, also generate 1-2 project-specific personas from it and from `## Brand Commitments`.
Skip this step if the Setup slug was null (vague or root-level target), and say why in one line of the close: "Not saved: critique one page, component or file to keep its history."

`max_score` is the applicable maximum from the heuristic table (40 when every heuristic applied), so a later run can tell a renormalized total from a full one. For a local file target, the helper also records an exact content fingerprint so polish can distinguish the assessed bytes from later edits without relying on Git state or timestamps. The helper prints the absolute path it wrote, and sometimes one more line (`Saved to Impeccable: <link>`, `Not saved to Impeccable: <reason>` or `Keep this critique's history: impeccable login`); put that line in the close word for word. Leave that file on disk. Polish closes it; this run does not. `REPORTS OFF:` instead means the project opted out of saved reports: skip the trend read and carry on.

This is fire-and-forget. Do not show the user the helper's JSON output; only the human-readable trend line, the written path, and the helper's Impeccable line. Failures here should not block the rest of the flow; print the error and move on.

- Skipping is allowed only when the report listed **fewer than 3 Priority Issues**, or on a read-only or delegated run. Count them; do not judge the findings "straightforward" by feel. At 3 or more on an interactive run, the questions are required.

**Final-question gate.** The user-visible response must either include the targeted questions or carry the literal line `Questions skipped: <reason>` naming the count or the delegated run that permitted the skip. Each question must include 2-3 concrete answer options tied to the actual critique findings. Do not end with only open-ended questions, and do not end with neither: stopping after the report, having asked nothing and printed no skip line, is the most common way this command fails.

Assessment A scores against [critique-rubric.md](critique-rubric.md): the cognitive load checklist, the heuristic scoring guide, and the personas. The report uses the bands and severities below.

### Scoring the report

# "Unknown command". The sibling binary must also report the version in
# VERSION: it is gitignored, so a skill upgrade that copies files over this
# directory leaves the old engine in place. A local build of the same version
# passes, which is why it is not hashed. IMPECCABLE_BIN is the operator's
# explicit choice and is exec'd without a probe. The version-pinned cache and
# the download are verified against engine-checksums.txt (next to this
# script), never against anything published beside the binary; a
# <binary>.verified stamp holding the manifest digest and the binary's size
# skips rehashing until either changes or the binary is newer than the stamp.
# No path hashes on every run: hooks run this launcher on every edit.

# Space, tab and CR, made once: hooks run this launcher on every edit and turn
# end, and every process it starts before the engine costs real time on a busy
# Windows machine (#1237), so the hot path below sticks to shell builtins.
ws=$(printf ' \t\r')

# Sets $digest_out to the digest engine-checksums.txt records for engine
# version $1 and asset $2 (lines are "<version> <asset> <sha256>"), empty when
# there is none.
# A CR is a separator too (CRLF checkouts), and a last line with no newline
# still counts.
manifest_digest() {
  digest_out=""
  [ -f "$manifest" ] || return 0
  while IFS="$ws" read -r m_version m_asset m_sum _ || [ -n "$m_version" ]; do
    case "$m_version" in ''|'#'*) continue ;; esac
    if [ "$m_version" = "$1" ] && [ "$m_asset" = "$2" ]; then
      digest_out=$m_sum
      return 0
    fi
  done < "$manifest"
  return 0
}
# Sets $expected (and, on Windows on ARM, which runs x64 binaries,
# $expected_x64) from engine-checksums.txt.
read_expected() {
  manifest_digest "$version" "$asset"
  expected=$digest_out
  expected_x64=""
  if [ "$os" = windows ] && [ "$arch" = arm64 ]; then
    manifest_digest "$version" impeccable-windows-x64.exe
    expected_x64=$digest_out
  fi
}
# Sets $size to the byte count of the cached binary (BSD wc pads it).
cached_size() {
  size=$(wc -c < "$cached") || size=""
  size=${size##* }
}
# Sets $actual to the sha256 of $1, empty when no hash tool works.
hash_file() {
  actual=""
  if command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if digest=$(shasum -a 256 "$1" 2>/dev/null); then actual=${digest%% *}; fi
  elif command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    if digest=$(sha256sum "$1" 2>/dev/null); then actual=${digest%% *}; fi
  fi
}

# This script's directory without dirname or a subshell: what dirname "$0"
# gives, made absolute by a cd there and back.
case $0 in
  */*) dir=${0%/*} ;;
  *) dir=. ;;
esac
[ -n "$dir" ] || dir=/
caller_pwd=$PWD
CDPATH= cd -- "$dir" || { echo "impeccable: cannot enter the launcher directory $dir" >&2; exit 127; }
dir=$PWD
skill_dir=${dir%/*}
[ -n "$skill_dir" ] || skill_dir=/
cd -- "$caller_pwd" || { echo "impeccable: cannot return to $caller_pwd" >&2; exit 127; }
# VS Code syncs a plugin without the executable bit. Its hooks run this through
# sh, so restore the bit for the commands the skill runs directly (#1249).
[ -x "$0" ] || chmod +x "$0" 2>/dev/null || :
manifest="$dir/engine-checksums.txt"
: "${IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR:=$skill_dir}"

# Windows names itself in the environment, which saves a process there; one
# uname covers the rest. PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE is what impeccable.cmd reads,
# so both launchers pick the same cached engine (AMD64 under x64 Git Bash on
# ARM64, as uname -m reported before).
if [ "${OS:-}" = Windows_NT ]; then
  sys="Windows_NT ${PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE:-unknown}"
else
  sys=$(uname -sm 2>/dev/null) || sys="unknown unknown"
fi
case "${sys%% *}" in

version=""
[ -f "$dir/VERSION" ] && { IFS="$ws" read -r version _ < "$dir/VERSION" || :; }

# Lost the executable bit in transit (zip extraction, some copiers).
if [ -f "$bin" ] && { [ -x "$bin" ] || chmod +x "$bin" 2>/dev/null; }; then
  if [ -n "$probing" ] || [ -z "$version" ] || { probe_ok "$bin" && [ "$probe_version" = "$version" ]; }; then
    exec "$bin" "$@"
  fi
  echo "impeccable: skipping $bin: it reports engine ${probe_version:-unknown} but this skill pins $version; delete it to stop this warning" >&2

asset="impeccable-$os-$arch"
[ "$os" = windows ] && asset="$asset.exe"

read_expected
  cached_size
  stamp=""
  stamp_size=""
  { IFS="$ws" read -r stamp stamp_size _ < "$cached.verified"; } 2>/dev/null || :
  if [ -n "$stamp" ] && [ "$stamp_size" = "$size" ] && { [ "$stamp" = "$expected" ] || [ "$stamp" = "$expected_x64" ]; } && [ ! "$cached" -nt "$cached.verified" ]; then
    exec "$cached" "$@"
  fi
  hash_file "$cached"
  if [ -n "$actual" ] && { [ "$actual" = "$expected" ] || [ "$actual" = "$expected_x64" ]; }; then
    { echo "$actual $size" > "$cached.verified"; } 2>/dev/null || :
    exec "$cached" "$@"
  fi
  echo "impeccable: cannot verify the cached engine $cached against $manifest; not using it" >&2

http_status=""
  download_host=""
rm -f "$download_file"

read_expected
  # Fail closed before any network traffic or cache write.
  if [ -z "$expected" ] && [ -z "$expected_x64" ]; then
    echo "impeccable: no checksum for engine $version ($asset) in $manifest; refusing the unverified download" >&2
    exit 127
  fi
cleanup() { rm -f "$tmp" 2>/dev/null || :; }
if [ -n "$expected" ] && fetch_url "$url"; then
elif [ -n "$expected_x64" ]; then
expected=$expected_x64

# No sha256 tool refuses the download too.
    hash_file "$tmp"
if [ -z "$actual" ]; then
echo "impeccable: cannot verify $url (no sha256 tool, or hashing failed); refusing the unverified download" >&2

cached_size
    { echo "$actual $size" > "$cached.verified"; } 2>/dev/null || :

@echo off
setlocal
rem Impeccable launcher (Windows). Runs bin\windows-<arch>\impeccable.exe next
rem to this file, else a cached or freshly downloaded engine binary.
rem
rem Structure notes (this file is exercised by dry parsing and string-level
rem tests, not yet on a real Windows machine):
rem - No multi-line parenthesized blocks: cmd expands %var% at block parse
rem   time, which made the old download path read back empty %url%/%cached%.
rem   Linear goto flow keeps every expansion on its own line, and avoids
rem   delayed expansion eating ! characters in user arguments.
rem - The unversioned user binary and the PATH candidate are validated with
rem   the engine-probe handshake (see :probe) so the retired 3.x npm CLI,
rem   whose bin is also named impeccable, is never exec'd. The sibling binary
rem   must also report the version in VERSION: it is not tracked, so a skill
rem   upgrade can leave an old engine in place. IMPECCABLE_BIN stays trusted.
rem - Downloads and the version-pinned cache are verified via certutil
rem   against engine-checksums.txt next to this file, and fail closed; a
rem   .verified stamp lets later runs skip hashing the cache while it holds
rem   the manifest digest and the binary's size and is not older than the
rem   binary. On ARM64 the arm64 asset is tried first and the x64 asset is the
rem   fallback (Windows on ARM runs x64 binaries), each only when the manifest
rem   has a line for it.
if not defined IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR set "IMPECCABLE_SKILL_DIR=%~dp0.."
if not defined IMPECCABLE_SELF set "IMPECCABLE_SELF=%~f0"
set "arch=x64"
if /I "%PROCESSOR_ARCHITECTURE%"=="ARM64" set "arch=arm64"

if not defined IMPECCABLE_BIN goto no_env_bin
if not exist "%IMPECCABLE_BIN%" goto no_env_bin
set "run=%IMPECCABLE_BIN%"
goto run
:no_env_bin

set "version="
if exist "%~dp0VERSION" set /p version=<"%~dp0VERSION"
set "bin=%~dp0bin\windows-%arch%\impeccable.exe"
if not exist "%bin%" goto no_sibling
if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE goto sibling_ok
if not defined version goto sibling_ok
call :probe "%bin%"
if "%probe_version%"=="%version%" goto sibling_ok
if not defined probe_version set "probe_version=unknown"
echo impeccable: skipping "%bin%": it reports engine %probe_version% but this skill pins %version%; delete it to stop this warning 1>&2
goto no_sibling
:sibling_ok
set "run=%bin%"
goto run
:no_sibling

set "home_bin=%USERPROFILE%\.impeccable\bin\impeccable.exe"
if not exist "%home_bin%" goto no_home_bin
if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE goto no_home_bin
call :probe "%home_bin%"
if not "%probe_ok%"=="1" goto no_home_bin
set "run=%home_bin%"
goto run
:no_home_bin

if not defined IMPECCABLE_HOME set "IMPECCABLE_HOME=%USERPROFILE%\.impeccable"
set "cached=%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%\impeccable.exe"
set "asset=impeccable-windows-%arch%.exe"
set "manifest=%~dp0engine-checksums.txt"
if not defined version goto no_cache
if not exist "%cached%" goto no_cache
call :read_expected
for %%f in ("%cached%") do set "size=%%~zf"
set "stamp="
if exist "%cached%.verified" for /f "usebackq tokens=1,2" %%s in ("%cached%.verified") do set "stamp=%%s"& set "stamp_size=%%t"
if not defined stamp goto cache_hash
if not "%stamp_size%"=="%size%" goto cache_hash
if /I "%stamp%"=="%expected%" goto cache_stamp_matches
if /I "%stamp%"=="%expected_x64%" goto cache_stamp_matches
goto cache_hash
:cache_stamp_matches
rem Newest first: the stamp must be listed before the binary it vouches for.
set "newest="
for /f "delims=" %%f in ('dir /b /a:-d /o:-d "%cached%*" 2^>nul') do if not defined newest set "newest=%%f"
if /I "%newest%"=="impeccable.exe.verified" goto cache_trusted
:cache_hash
call :sha256 "%cached%" "%TEMP%\impeccable-hash-%RANDOM%%RANDOM%.txt"
if not defined actual goto cache_unverified
if /I "%actual%"=="%expected%" goto cache_verified
if /I "%actual%"=="%expected_x64%" goto cache_verified
:cache_unverified
echo impeccable: cannot verify the cached engine "%cached%" against "%manifest%"; not using it 1>&2
goto no_cache
:cache_verified
(>"%cached%.verified" echo %actual% %size%) 2>nul
:cache_trusted
set "run=%cached%"
goto run
:no_cache

if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE goto download
rem The first impeccable on PATH, resolved once so the probe and the run see
rem the same file. A batch shim (npm writes impeccable.cmd) must run under
rem call to return here (#1240), and call expands % in the arguments a second
rem time; a real binary runs directly so a target such as a%20b reaches it intact.
set "path_bin="
rem where also lists npm's extensionless POSIX shim, which cmd cannot run:
rem take the first match with a runnable extension.
rem Loop letters c and k are not path modifiers, so %%~xc reads as the
rem extension of c and never as a loop variable followed by text.
for /f "delims=" %%c in ('where impeccable 2^>nul') do if not defined path_bin for %%k in (.exe .com .cmd .bat) do if /I "%%~xc"=="%%k" set "path_bin=%%c"
if not defined path_bin goto download
call :probe "%path_bin%"
if not "%probe_ok%"=="1" goto download
for %%k in ("%path_bin%") do set "path_ext=%%~xk"
if /I "%path_ext%"==".cmd" goto path_shim
if /I "%path_ext%"==".bat" goto path_shim
"%path_bin%" %*
exit /b %errorlevel%
:path_shim
call "%path_bin%" %*
exit /b %errorlevel%

:download
rem Last resort: fetch this version's binary from the release channel into
rem the version-pinned user cache, verify it, then run it. Never inside
rem another launcher's probe: fail fast and quiet instead.
if defined IMPECCABLE_LAUNCHER_PROBE exit /b 127
if not defined version goto fail
call :read_expected
if not defined expected if not defined expected_x64 goto no_checksum
where curl.exe >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 goto curl_missing
if not defined IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE set "IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE=https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable/releases/download"
if exist "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%\" goto cache_ready
mkdir "%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%" >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 goto cache_directory_failed
:cache_ready
rem Stage the download in a directory only this run owns, as the sh launcher
rem does with .impeccable.part.$$: concurrent first runs (parallel hooks, two
rem agents) must never write, hash or move each other's files. mkdir fails
rem when the name exists, so it claims the name atomically. RANDOM alone is
rem not enough because cmd seeds it from the clock in whole seconds; the
rem timestamp and the retry on collision keep same-second runs apart. A cache
rem directory that refuses every mkdir is reported as unwritable.
set "attempt=0"
:claim_staging
set /a attempt+=1
if %attempt% GTR 20 goto cache_write_failed
set "stamp=%TIME: =0%"
set "stamp=%stamp::=%"
set "stamp=%stamp:.=%"
set "stamp=%stamp:,=%"
set "staging=%IMPECCABLE_HOME%\bin\%version%\.impeccable.part.%stamp%-%RANDOM%%RANDOM%"
mkdir "%staging%" >nul 2>nul
if errorlevel 1 goto claim_staging
set "part=%staging%\impeccable.exe"
rem Redirection failures do not reliably update ERRORLEVEL in cmd.exe;
rem branch on the command's failure directly.
(type nul >"%part%") 2>nul || goto staging_write_failed
set "url=%IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE%/engine-v%version%/%asset%"
if not defined expected goto fetch_x64
call :fetch_url
if not errorlevel 1 goto verify
:fetch_x64
if not defined expected_x64 goto download_failed
set "asset=impeccable-windows-x64.exe"
set "expected=%expected_x64%"
set "url=%IMPECCABLE_DOWNLOAD_BASE%/engine-v%version%/%asset%"
call :fetch_url
if errorlevel 1 goto download_failed

:verify
call :check_download
if errorlevel 1 exit /b 127
rem Mirrors the sh launcher and fails closed: a freshly downloaded binary
rem runs only after its hash matches the digest read from engine-checksums.txt.
rem An empty certutil result refuses the download instead of running an

# Critique rubric

Assessment A's rubric in [critique.md](critique.md): cognitive load, the heuristic scores, and personas. The score bands and P0 to P3 severity stay in critique.md, where the report uses them.
If PRODUCT.md has a `## Users` section (written by `impeccable init`), derive 1–2 additional personas from it and from `## Brand Commitments`:
**Profile**: [2-3 key characteristics derived from PRODUCT.md]
Only generate project-specific personas when PRODUCT.md describes real users. Don't invent audience details; use the 5 predefined personas when no context exists.
